lead: Arsenal Image Mounter makes a forensic disk image show up in Windows as a real disk, so other tools and programs can use it. It is made by Arsenal Recon and runs in a free mode when no licence is installed.
use_when: You have an E01 or raw image and want Windows to treat it as a disk, without making a full copy first.
You want to read an image without any change, or let a program write to it while the changes go to a side file.
You want a disk that a virtual machine program can use, to see the system as the user saw it.

features.title: Free mode, as listed on the vendor page
items: Shows raw, forensic and virtual machine images to Windows as complete disks
Temporary writes that go to difference files you can replay
Saves a mounted object to several disk image formats
Finds, unlocks and can fully decrypt BitLocker volumes, or turn BitLocker off or pause it
Exposes disks, volumes and Volume Shadow Copies as virtual dd files

features.title: More in free mode
items: Command line programs and PowerShell modules
Fake disk signatures, MBR injection and removable disk emulation
Virtual mounting of optical images and archives, and RAM disks

features.title: Professional mode, as listed on the vendor page
items: Starts virtual machines from disk images, physical disks and remote disks
Bypasses Windows sign-in, DPAPI and S Mode inside the virtual machine, and Linux passwords too
Mounts Volume Shadow Copies in several ways, and can launch VMs from them
Writes a mounted image out to a physical disk
Bypasses the Windows file system driver for several file systems, and exposes NTFS metadata, slack and unallocated space

features.title: Mount options shown in published tutorials
items: Read only: no writes are allowed
Write temporary: writes go to a separate difference file and the image stays unchanged
Write original: writes go straight into the image, so avoid it on evidence
Fake disk signature, sector size and a removable disk option

formats: Forensic images such as E01 (shown in tutorials)
requirements: It runs on Windows. The vendor pages name no other platform and list no versions. A tutorial notes that the VM program had to run as administrator. The downloads page says antivirus software may flag the tools because of obfuscation, so ask your lab or tutor before changing antivirus settings. The page also says versions from 3.11.290 on changed the licensing.

steps.title: Download it
steps.text: Use the download link on this page, which leads to the Arsenal Recon downloads page. At the time of checking, the current build was hosted on Mega. Download it only from the vendor's page.

steps.title: Install and start it as administrator
steps.text: Install it and start the program. With no licence it opens in free mode. Write down the version you use in your notes.

steps.title: Choose the image
steps.text: Use the mount image button or the File menu entry for mounting an image, then pick your E01 or raw file.

steps.title: Pick a mount option
steps.text: For viewing only, choose Read only. If a program must write, such as a virtual machine, choose Write temporary and, if offered, choose where the difference file goes. Do not choose Write original on evidence.

steps.title: Check the new disk
steps.text: The image appears in the main window as a disk. Open Disk Management or diskpart to see its disk number. A tutorial for VMware also sets the disk offline, so Windows itself does not write to it.

steps.title: Use the disk
steps.text: Open it with your analysis tool, or add it to a virtual machine program as a physical disk. A published tutorial does this with VMware Workstation and turns the VM network off. Keep notes of every step.

steps.title: Remove the mounted image
steps.text: Select the image and use the remove button, or remove all. Then delete or keep the difference file as your lab procedure says, and check the image hash is unchanged.

cases.title: Read-only look at an image
cases.why: A mounted read-only disk lets you browse folders in Windows or open the disk in other tools.

cases.title: Running a tool that needs a real disk
cases.why: Some programs only accept a physical disk. Mounting as a disk makes the image look like one.

cases.title: Seeing the user's desktop
cases.why: A write-temporary disk can be given to a virtual machine program so the old system starts, with changes kept in a side file.

cases.title: BitLocker images
cases.why: The vendor page says free mode can identify and unlock BitLocker volumes. You still need the key or password.

cases.title: Practice and teaching
cases.why: The free mode lets students try mounting, offline disks and virtual machine boots without buying a licence.

strengths: Free mode covers whole-disk mounting and temporary writes, as the vendor page lists.
The source code is published under a dual licence: AGPL v3 or a separate licence from Arsenal Recon.
It has command line and PowerShell support, so mounting can be scripted.
Published tutorials show it working with VMware Workstation and, through Imm2Virtual, with VirtualBox.
limits: Starting a virtual machine directly from an image is a Professional mode feature on the vendor page. In free mode you attach the disk to the VM program yourself.
The vendor pages do not list every image format. Test your format before relying on it.
Write original changes the image. Pick it by mistake and the evidence is changed.
Antivirus programs may flag it, and licence rules changed in later versions, so read the downloads page.
A mounted disk can still fail to boot in a VM because of controller, UEFI, driver or BitLocker problems. The tool does not fix these.

works_with.note: Create the E01 first, or mount images another way
Verify or export E01 files, or mount them on Linux
Analyse the same image in a full case tool
